precepts.text: When they had prayed, the place was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness. When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God and they could prove it.
precepts.point: Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. But Peter, standing up with the eleven, said, these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day. But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel: in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. Prophesy about what? The gathering of the twelve tribes of Israel; teaching the people who they are. The masses did not know; it was the job of the priests and the prophets to teach the people. But in the last days God is raising the message back up, and we are going out to raise our people back up and show them they are not Arabs and Muslims and African Americans or whatever label was put on them: we are the children of Israel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
On the day of Pentecost “suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting”, and “they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.” That Holy Ghost was the mighty wind that filled them.

Acts 4 shows the same thing again: “And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.” The place shook, the Holy Ghost filled them, and the result was boldness.

When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold in what they said, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God, and they could prove it from the scriptures. That is the spirit that came on them at Pentecost: not a show, but a boldness to speak the word of God, grounded in knowing it.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
The believers in Acts 4 “were of one heart and of one soul” and “had all things common”. To keep from losing ourselves, selling ourselves out and losing our souls, we have to grow the same way. Paul shows what pulls us away: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

The seducing spirits are money and wealth, the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the blitz last week, kids said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that actually build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. And there are men and women in the faith who want to leave this and go to the world and stream.

The “doctrines of devils” are religion, man-made religion. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy” is politics: a lie that makes you feel assimilated into a government that is kicking you out of it. If you are Israel, what they call black, you cannot be in their government. There is one black governor in this whole country, and all the black generals have been taken out as not qualified. They are making their country great again in their eyes.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.” Religion, politics and the gifts of this world sear the conscience. Money, riches and comfort should not be your god; the American dream is a lie. Having all things in common, in faith and understanding, is what keeps us from departing from the faith.

precepts.text: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves: going for likes and followers, me, me, me, when it is not about you, it is about your people. Covetous, boasters of vanity, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection: this is the nature of them that go after the world, after the gift that destroys the heart.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to start having all things in common, like the believers of Acts 4, and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society or your community. It is me, me, me: how many likes and followers do I have? It is not about you, negro. It is about your people. “Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy, Without natural affection”.

This is the nature of them that go after the world, that go after the gift that destroys the heart. The one who is a lover of himself holds on to what he has; the believers in Acts 4 said none of the things they possessed was their own.

So we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and content in life. A family of seven may need a house with a little room, but if you are a single brother, why are you buying a mansion and expensive cars? Do you know the times we are living in? There is coming a time when you will not be worrying about maintaining your BMW. Riches and comfort, keeping up with the Joneses and the American lie of a dream, should not be your god.

precepts.why:
The same chapter shows what having all things common looked like: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

That is the point. We have to begin to live below our means, not beyond them. This nation of ours is a big nation, and there are millions of our people that lack. When you sacrifice your much, it is much to them that have little.

The only way to experience that, to let what you have help those who have little, is to travel. We must go and spread this gospel abroad, and that is part of why we go out into the nations.

The believers of Acts 4 had prayed, the place was shaken, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and spake the word with boldness. Out of that came one heart and one soul, and out of one heart and one soul came a people among whom no one lacked. That is the same order we need now: faith first, and then a nation that looks after its own.

precepts.point: They commanded the apostles not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus. It will happen in America too.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
The rulers “commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus”, and again: “Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name?” We read that and say it could never happen in America. Don't fool yourself. It will happen here.

Christ warned it: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” Imagine they shut your bank account down. Now you can't pay your rent, your mortgage, your car note; you lose your car, your home, and maybe your wife: that's what you get for teaching that Bible, don't block Jesus. Everybody says, I'm strong, I can go through it. Wait till that day, with a newborn baby and you can't get infant formula. Some will say, I'm going back to being a Christian so I can get access to my money.

That hatred starts with the followers of Christ, but it applies to all twelve tribes of Israel. Look at the news: black and brown people killed, and they cry, what did we do to these white people? Why did they kill Sandra Bland? Why did they kill Tamir Rice? Christ said you would be hated of all nations. Christ is our king whether you accept it or not, and the white man looks at you and says, these are the people of Christ. You are the children of God, and they are the children of the devil. You might not like it, but it's true.

precepts.text: If they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.
precepts.point: They commanded the apostles not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus. It will happen in America too.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
Being hated of all nations is not only for those who teach the Bible; Ezra shows who it will affect. “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was paradise in the time of Adam. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

You have to enter those hard things to enter paradise. The angel is telling Ezra that if we don't go through the hardships of Jacob's trouble, we can never get paradise. If you decide to kill yourself before it happens, you cannot get paradise. If you say, I'm going to join another religion to escape punishment from these other nations, you will never receive it.

Read on: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. The righteous shall suffer hard things, that is Jacob's trouble, and hope for paradise. “for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The wicked Israelites are going through Jacob's trouble too, but they are not going to see the kingdom.

So when Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, it covers all Israel. Whether you teach or not, the strait things are coming; the only question is whether you come out of them into what is laid up for you. That is why you cannot run from the persecution when they command us not to teach in his name.

precepts.text: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be.
precepts.point: They commanded the apostles not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus. It will happen in America too.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
“And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad”. We saw persecution against our brothers in France; it hasn't gotten here yet, and they say America is the major hub. When it happens, can you stand the rain? That's why we say don't take the convocations lightly.

People read these things and say, oh, that's old time. But Solomon says: “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” That's you and me. We read Maccabees and Acts 8:1 and say that could never happen again? You're simple as hell. What happened in 1 Maccabees 1 and Daniel 3 is what Revelation 13 speaks of, no buying and selling, and it leads to death.

Paul said the same thing: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Those old-time things were written for us to learn from, because they are going to happen again. We need patience and the comfort of the scriptures because we are going to go through what our ancestors went through: how did they deal with it, how did they survive?

Herod killed James and, because it pleased them, took Peter also. And Trump joked about bringing back public executions. The Christians don't understand what is about to come; in here we understand, because what has been is what shall be.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.” Peter and John show that boldness: “Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.”

They were perceived as unlearned men, yet their boldness made men take knowledge that they had been with Christ, who taught as one having authority. The boldness came from being with him.

We can be bold this same way by using the words of the Most High, which no one can gainsay. That is the righteous bold as a lion: not learning or standing, but the words of the Most High in the mouth.

“For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.”

The Sadducees were grieved that the apostles preached the resurrection, and they did not even believe in it. They were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions.

They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people.

Christ answered, “Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.”

That is the same thing Christians and five-percenters do: take our scriptures that they reject and use them to try to confound us. And it is the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures.
